# Antigens and antibodies, immune response

## 1. Introduction
Opening frame for **Antigens and antibodies** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Human Health and Diseases fill pass.

## 2. Hierarchy body — every syllabus sub-point
### Antigens and antibodies
### immune response

Fill order per concept: definition → structure → process → significance (§3.2). Step-by-step numbered points, Pioneer style.

An **antigen** is any substance that the immune system recognises as foreign and reacts against (toxin, protein on a pathogen surface, pollen). An **antibody (immunoglobulin)** is the Y-shaped protein a plasma B cell secretes to bind that antigen specifically. Antibodies never kill directly — they tag: neutralise toxins, coat pathogens for phagocytes (opsonisation), clump them (agglutination), or trigger complement.

**Concept flow — from antigen encounter to immune memory (study in this order)**

| Step | Event | Key cell / molecule |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Antigen enters and is captured | Macrophage / dendritic cell presents it |
| 2 | Helper T cell activates the right clone | CD4 helper T + interleukins |
| 3 | B cells divide into plasma cells | Clonal selection and expansion |
| 4 | Antibodies flood the blood (primary response) | IgM first, then IgG |
| 5 | Antigen cleared; most plasma cells die | Feedback shuts the response off |
| 6 | Memory B and T cells persist | Years of protection |
| 7 | Re-exposure → fast, massive secondary response | IgG dominated, no illness |

**The five antibody classes — classified by structure and role**

| Class | Structure | Where found | Main role |
|---|---|---|---|
| IgG | Monomer | Blood, tissue fluid, crosses placenta | Main defender of secondary response; gives newborn passive immunity |
| IgM | Pentamer (5 Y units) | Blood — first on the scene | First antibody of the primary response; powerful agglutinator |
| IgA | Dimer (2 Y units) | Tears, saliva, milk, gut mucus | Mucosal defence; protects the newborn via colostrum |
| IgE | Monomer | Mast cells and basophils | Allergy and anti-parasite response; triggers histamine release |
| IgD | Monomer | B cell surface | B cell receptor — antigen recognition |

**Primary vs secondary immune response; active vs passive immunity**

| Feature | Primary response | Secondary response |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | First meeting with the antigen | Re-exposure to the same antigen |
| Lag period | 5–7 days or more | 1–2 days |
| Main antibody | IgM, then some IgG | Massive IgG |
| Magnitude | Moderate, short-lived | Much larger, long-lasting |
| Driving cells | Naive B cells | Memory B cells |

## 6. Key terms and statements
Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).

**Worked example — reading an antibody titre.** A patient's blood shows high IgM against a virus but almost no IgG: the infection is **new** (primary response). A second sample two weeks later shows IgM falling and IgG rising steeply: the patient is clearing the infection and has gained memory. If the first sample already had high IgG with no IgM, the infection was old or the patient was vaccinated — IgG tells history, IgM tells news.

## 8. Summary and self-check
5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.

**Summary.** Antigens trigger clonal selection; antibodies are specific Y-shaped tags with five classes (GAMED) each suited to a compartment and a job. The primary response is slow IgM; the secondary is fast massive IgG from memory cells. **Self-check:** can you sketch the antibody and name which class responds first?

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Antigen = foreign molecule binding antibody/MHC; antibody = Y-shaped Ig (2 heavy + 2 light chains, disulphide bonds) with variable antigen-binding sites — draw the Y.
Trick 2: Ig classes: IgG (most abundant, crosses placenta), IgA (secretions), IgM (first response, pentamer), IgE (allergy), IgD — the five classes with one role each.
Trick 3: Primary vs secondary response: secondary is faster, stronger (memory cells) — the graph sketch earns marks.
Trick 4: Antibody actions: neutralisation, opsonisation, agglutination, complement lysis — four verbs, four marks.
